newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Costello says tax reform needed.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Costello says tax reform needed.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday the tax system needed reform.
When asked if the government needed to reform the taxation system, Costello told Adelaide radio: "We think we do."
He said some reform measures had already been put in place since the Liberal-National government came to power last March.

But Costello went on to say: "We have to get the burden of taxation down in this country if we are going to stay in league with our near neigbours in the Asia-Pacific region with whom we are now in competition."
"And so whatever the way you collect it the overall burden of taxation has to be low," Costello said, adding that the taxation burden had to be equally shared.
"I think people get concerned when they feel that -- look here's a company that can put assets in the Bahamas and doesn't seem to pay much tax and poor old me I have it taken out of my P.A.Y.E."

"So they are the two things that are driving me -- fairness and rates," he said, adding that those two elements had already been taken into account by the reforms that the government had put in place over the past 12 months.

Australian Prime Minister John Howard said in a television on the weekend that taxation reform was needed but declined to say whether the government would consider introducing a goods and services tax (GST).

The conservative Liberal/National government promised before the March 1996 election not to introduce a GST, but has since qualified that promise by saying it applied only to its first term of government.
